content:
Local weather is one of the most underrated variables to use in your Apple Home automation setup. Over the past few years, I have used sensors for everything from knowing when to drip faucets in freezing weather to adjusting the sprinkler schedule with the Eve Aqua on hot days. Eve Weather has been part of my setup for a while now, and with its Matter upgrade a few years ago, it is incredibly useful in my home.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

If you have read HomeKit Weekly for any amount of time, you know I love automations that just run on their own. Smart home accessories are only useful if they can do something automatically. That is exactly why I have always recommended building around a single ecosystem for your smart home instead of mixing and matching. Even in the age of Matter, I don’t want to use a bunch of different platforms. For me, that is Apple Home. I lean on Eve devices because they have always prioritized privacy and skipped the cloud account requirement if you simply stick to local control that works with Matter. Eve has also been aggressive in supporting Matter and Thread in recent years. That is what you want to see.

Eve Weather gives you three data points from a single small device: temperature, humidity, and air pressure. It is IPX4 water-resistant, and the aluminum body makes it look like it belongs right outside my house. That is exactly where mine is mounted. It gives me hyperlocal readings that are often a couple of degrees off from what the Apple Weather app reports. Honestly, that difference is critical depending on whether it is super hot or very cold. When your pipes freeze at 31°F and your app says 34°F, you will definitely wish you had the local data.

One of the underrated features of Eve Weather is its built-in 12-hour weather trend display. It uses changes in air pressure to predict what the weather will do. You get a visual icon showing if it is likely to be sunny, cloudy, rainy, or stormy. That little detail adds a lot of value, and it is something you can see at a glance without having to open an app on your phone.

Here are a few of the automations you could build using the Eve Weather:

  • Turn on a colored light when the temperature dips below freezing to remind the family to drip the faucets.
  • Trigger a dehumidifier when the outdoor humidity is especially high.
  • Delay the sprinkler system if it has already rained and the forecast indicates more rain is coming.
  • Ask Siri what the current front yard temperature is without going outside.

Matter and Thread support in 2026

A couple of years ago, Eve released a free firmware update to bring Matter support to Eve Weather. If you already own the device, you can upgrade it using the Eve app. The Matter version brought support for Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and SmartThings alongside Apple Home. It is the exact same sensor, just platform agnostic, which makes it future-proof if you ever decide to change your primary smart home ecosystem.

Eve Weather is what is called a Minimal Thread Device. That means it communicates over Thread but does not relay traffic. That job is for always-on Full Thread Devices like the Eve Energy or Eve Water Guard. The more Full Thread Devices you have, the stronger and more stable your Thread network becomes, and battery-powered devices like Eve Weather directly benefit from that stability.

You also still do not need an Eve account. Everything stays local unless you choose otherwise. The Eve iPhone app is a fantastic tool for visualizing and tracking historical temperature, pressure, and humidity trends. It is a really cool way to spot patterns and make smarter decisions about things like watering your lawn or managing energy usage.

I use some HomePod minis throughout the house and rely on my Eero 6E network to support Thread. Eero includes Thread support in its software, so it serves as a solid foundation for accessories like Eve Weather to stay connected and working fast.

Wrap up on Eve Weather

The only thing I would still love to see is a rechargeable battery. The battery lasts several months, but I would much prefer a USB-C port like the one the Eve Room uses. That said, Eve Weather is one of my favorite Apple Home accessories. It is simple, it looks great, and it works really well across all major platforms thanks to Matter. If you are looking to add local weather info to your smart home and trigger useful automations, the Eve Weather is an easy recommendation for me.

You can buy it from Amazon or directly from the Eve Store.
